rv.q: It does mean something to put Tannahill's play in the same august company as Bess Wohl's 'Liberation,' Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' 'Purpose' and Emil Weinstein's 'Becoming Eve,' all of which opened earlier this year.

Tannahill probes these feelings in a fresh and unexpected setting in Prince Faggot, with some clever twists, but his romantic fantasy, built around the classic tropes of a shocking love between prince and commoner and the conflict between desire and duty, all too often can't quite bear the weight of what he seeks to achieve.
